subject: Transportation Systems
title: Emergency Ventilation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Emergency Ventilation.

hook.text: If a fire breaks out underground, smoke fills a tunnel in minutes. Ventilation is the first defense.

buildup.text: Giant fans can push or pull air through tunnels, directing smoke away from passengers.

discovery.text: Modern systems reverse fan direction to create escape corridors of clean air.

twist.text: The 2003 Daegu fire in South Korea killed 192 people—partly because ventilation was inadequate.

climax.text: Since then, ventilation standards worldwide have become far stricter. Every new station is stress-tested.

punchline.text: Underground, air management is a matter of life and death.

quiz.question: Why is subway ventilation critical during emergencies?
options: To direct smoke away from passengers
